column3: Private IP Disclosure - the docs pages ship literal private addresses (127.0.0.1, 172.17.0.0/16 docker-bridge, unix-socket examples) as configuration samples for a Docker socket proxy. They are documentation content, not this deployment's infrastructure leaking through response headers or errors.

Re-examine Cache-control Directives (informational) - advisory to review cache-control, not a finding. The static export's caching (immutable hashed assets, revalidated HTML) is set deliberately at the Vercel edge; the deliberate 10049 suppression already records that threat model.

Storable and Cacheable Content (informational) - www.getsockguard.com serves content-hashed static assets (/_next/static/**) with Cache-Control: public,max-age=31536000,immutable. That is the intended threat model for hashed bundle filenames (verified 2026-08-17), not a vulnerability; matches the same suppression in drydock's .zap/rules.tsv.

Retrieved from Cache (informational) - responses are served from Vercel's CDN, so ZAP sees Age/X-Vercel-Cache headers. Expected for a statically-hosted marketing+docs site with no per-user or sensitive content.

CSP script-src unsafe-inline - accepted: a Next.js static export (next export, no server to mint per-request nonces) inlines its hydration/bootstrap scripts, so a nonce/hash-only script-src isn't achievable without abandoning static hosting. The site serves only public content and runs no first-party inline event handlers on user-controllable data. Mirrors drydock's 10055 suppression (theirs style-src, same root cause).

Cross-Domain Misconfiguration - the permissive CORS ZAP flags is on public static assets (fonts, /_next/static/**) served from the CDN. The site has no authenticated or credentialed endpoints, so a wildcard ACAO exposes nothing an anonymous fetch of the same public URL wouldn't already return.
Modern Web Application (informational) - SPA/JS-app detection notice, not a finding; recurs on every scan. Mirrors drydock's 10109 suppression.

Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy Header Missing - COEP is an opt-in cross-origin isolation feature, not a baseline requirement; the site needs no crossOriginIsolated context (no SharedArrayBuffer/precise timers), and require-corp would break legitimate CDN/font subresource loads. Not setting it is the intended posture, not a vulnerability.
